The original square has side length \( s \) and area \( s^2 \).  
After the changes, one pair of opposite sides becomes \( 0.6s \) (decreased by 40%) and the other pair becomes \( 1.5s \) (increased by 50%).  
The area of the resulting rectangle is \( 0.6s \times 1.5s = 0.9s^2 \).  
This is 90% of the original area, so the area decreases by \( 10\% \).

Answer: 10%
